text:
Maya G: Heads up — saw a regen in p95 token throughput after last kernel-selector tweak. Putting notes here for batch/token-cap tuning.
Arjun P: repro steps?
Maya G: load test on mixed-cluster (A100 + A10 hot nodes). End-to-end p95 per-request jumped ~18% on conversational workload with KV hits ~60%.
Zane: did kernel fallback increase? might be picking an L4-optimized kernel on A100 in some shapes.
Maya G: exactly. profiler shows kernel-selection flip on sequences ~1024-1280 and batch formation sometimes packs fewer requests -> lower batch tokens.
perf-bot: perf/regression alert: job id 2026-03-17-rls-47. baseline p95=124ms -> current p95=146ms, token-ops/sec -12%.
Leah: can you paste the profiler snippet and batching config you used?
Maya G: profiler excerpt:
```
kernel_selector: chosen_kernel="kv-stream-v2" (fit_score=0.78)
seq_len=1200 batch_size=6 packed_tokens=7200 kv_frag=0.34 kernel_time=0.098s other=0.004s
fallbacks: l4-tiling (attempted)
```
Maya G: batcher config we ran (simplified):
```
queue.max_wait_ms: 12
batcher.max_batch_tokens: 8192
batcher.max_batch_items: 8
token_bucket.refill_rate: 5000 tokens/s
```
Arjun P: mixed-cluster policy likely routing smaller shapes to kernels optimized for shorter sequences. That reduces kernel-fit for long sequences and increases fragmentation of KV cache which kills throughput.
Zane: agree. We should try per-GPU token budget caps and kernel-fit thresholds so A100 prefers kernels that scale with larger packed_tokens.
Leah: propose a quick mapping I sketched for max_batch_tokens (per GPU family):
- T4: 4096
- L4: 6144
- A10: 8192
- A100: 12288
- H100: 16384
Leah: rationale: memory bandwidth + kernel tiling sweet spots + kv-frag tolerance.
Maya G: that looks reasonable. Also suggest lowering queue.max_wait_ms to 8ms on T4/L4 to avoid holding small lat-sensitive requests.
Arjun P: we need a runbook for experiments. Steps: 1) pin kernel-selector v2 vs v1 2) apply per-GPU max_batch_tokens mapping 3) run mixed-cluster load with KV-hit ratios {10,40,70}% 4) capture p50/p95/p99 and kernel switch counts 5) check KV fragmentation metric (kv_frag) and cold-starts.
Maya G: adding a small adaptive step: if kv_frag > 0.45 then temporarily reduce max_batch_tokens by 15% on that cardclass to force better packing shapes.
Zane: good safety. Also add a kernel-fit soft-threshold: require fit_score >= 0.70 for chosen kernel on A100/H100 for sequences >1024, otherwise prefer larger-kernel path.
Leah: quick config prototype for token-budget-policy: 
```
per_gpu:
  A100:
    max_batch_tokens: 12288
    min_kernel_fit: 0.7
    frag_threshold: 0.45
  A10:
    max_batch_tokens: 8192
    min_kernel_fit: 0.6
    frag_threshold: 0.5
  L4:
    max_batch_tokens: 6144
    min_kernel_fit: 0.55
    frag_threshold: 0.5
  T4:
    max_batch_tokens: 4096
    min_kernel_fit: 0.5
    frag_threshold: 0.55
  H100:
    max_batch_tokens: 16384
    min_kernel_fit: 0.75
    frag_threshold: 0.4
```
Maya G: we should also instrument a new metric: kernel_switch_rate per 10k requests. If it spikes when enabling mapping, roll back.
Arjun P: small nit — these tokens budgets assume average token size. For models with long KV keys or function-calls, pack efficiency drops. We should surface a model-specific pack_factor and compute effective_max = floor(max_batch_tokens * pack_factor).
Zane: test plan timeline: today run A100-only baseline with new policy, tomorrow run mixed cluster. I can schedule a 2x 1hr load window.
Leah: I can add observability: per-route charts for packed_tokens distribution, kv_frag, kernel_choice histogram, kernel_switch_rate.
Maya G: one more: consider soft-eviction TTL for KV cache entries older than 60s under high frag to free slots for hot prefixes. That helped earlier.
Arjun P: ack. Also let's capture tail-cost delta (tokens/s saved) to ensure we don't regress cost per token with larger batches.
perf-bot: scheduled test windows: 17:00UTC A100-only run, 01:00UTC mixed-run. Test ids: run-223, run-224.
Maya G: thanks — I'll push a prototype config to canary and post results in this thread after A100 run. :thumbsup:
Leah: ping me when canary is up, I'll wire dashboards.
Zane: I'll own the kernel-selector telemetry validation.
Maya G: final note — keep an eye on latency SLO breaches when changing max_batch_tokens; higher token caps can increase p99 if batching delay grows. We'll favor p95 cost wins only if p99 stays bounded.
ops-bot: deploy-notice: canary config change queued for 1700UTC.
Maya G: thanks team, will update with numbers shortly.
